Triage: lands in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` (`registerMetadataEndpoints`); `domain:cli`. → `pm:queue`, Bug — premise re-verified on `origin/main`: `POST /meta/:type/:name/publish` is mounted single-arity only (rest-server.ts:5936) while the `published` read is mounted in both arities (rest-server.ts:6389), and #11712's landed fix (PR #11933) did not touch the promote door. Mechanism assumption for the dev to verify, not a ruling relay: the card cites #7019/#7526 as the twin-parity precedent — re-read both before implementing. Clause-②: **yes** (a newly mounted route expands the public surface) — the claim must declare it and dispatch runs at the contract-review tier. Watch the route-ordering trap already documented at rest-server.ts:6291 (compound segments vs literal suffixes) for `publish` collisions.

Branch: `claude/issue-11932-compound-publish-door`.
Declared file surface: `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` (`registerMetadataEndpoints`) + its pins + a changeset.

**Serial released by the merge.** This card was fenced behind PR #11985 (`rest-server.ts`), which **merged 2026-08-25T05:42Z**. The merge releases a serial, not the arming. ⚠️ **#11718 and #11473 land in this same file and are deliberately NOT dispatched** — they queue behind this card and are released when it merges.

**Clause ②: yes**, per triage `5404244362` and re-affirmed here — **mounting a new route expands the public surface**, which is the mechanical test's clearest case. `needs:contract-review` hung on the card in this stroke and read back; hang it on the PR the moment the PR exists. ⛔ This seat does not clear it — the chain does, and it records its verdict **on this card**.

### Where this card came from, and why the gap is real rather than theoretical

#11712's dev found this while landing PR #11933 and **filed it rather than widening that PR** — the right call, and the reason it is a separate card. #11933's changeset now names the gap in as many words:

> The draft you can now stage has no per-item REST promotion door in this arity. Until that route exists, promote through `POST /packages/:id/publish-drafts` (whole-package) or the runtime dispatcher's own `meta.publish` verb. Tracked in #11932.

So a consumer reading release notes has already been told this hole exists. **Closing it is what lets that paragraph come out of the next changeset**, which is a concrete completion condition rather than a vague improvement.

The asymmetry, measured on `origin/main` before #11933 landed and re-verified by triage after:

```
read:     for (const publishedPath of [ `${metaPath}/:type/:name/published`,
                                        `${metaPath}/:type/:section/:name/published` ])   ← BOTH arities
promote:  path: `${metaPath}/:type/:name/publish`                                          ← ONE arity
```

`publishMetaItem` itself promotes a compound name fine — **it is the route that is missing, not the capability.** Verify that yourself before building on it.

⛔ **Re-derive every offset.** Triage measured `rest-server.ts:5936` (promote) and `:6389` (published read) — but **#11985 landed in this exact file after that**, so both have moved. Publish the commands and raw output. In R35 this seat handed devs stale numbers **five times** and measurement moved them every time; ⛔ do not reconcile to anything above.

### ⚠️ The named trap — route ordering

Triage points at the ordering hazard already documented in this file (near the old `:6291`):

> Registered BEFORE the compound `/:type/:section/:name/published` … the three-segment form collides with it exactly the way `/history` and `/audit` do, and **Hono is first-match-wins**.

A compound `…/:type/:section/:name/publish` has the same shape and the same collision risk against `/:type/:section/:name`. **Pin the ordering, not just the route** — a test that only asserts the new route answers can pass while a differently-ordered registration silently shadows something else. Show what would break if it were registered in the wrong place.

### Precedent to re-read, ⛔ not to relay

Triage names #7019 and #7526 as the twin-parity precedent and explicitly calls it *"a mechanism assumption for the dev to verify, not a ruling relay"*. Re-read both. ⭐ #11712's fork clause is the model for how this ends: if the measurement says a compound promote door **cannot** work — some keying, ordering or authorization reason — that is a **reportable result**, not a licence to ship nothing quietly and not a reason to force it through. Report the fork on this card.

### Anti-vacuity

- Drive the **real registered handler** through `RestServer.getRoutes()` over the real protocol — never a stand-in. #11933's pins are next door and are the shape to follow.
- ⭐ **Assert what the write DID, not just the status.** #11712's whole defect was a door that accepted a parameter and answered `200` while doing the wrong thing; a status-only pin cannot see that class. Read the store: a promoted compound draft must actually become live.
- Add a **door-to-door parity pin that is literal-free on both sides** — assert the compound and single-segment doors agree without naming either's status, so a future move on either side reddens independently (#11731 §4 / #11933 §5 precedent).
- Show every pin failing without the behaviour: revert only your source change, keep the pins, run. Confirm the mutation **on disk with anchored greps in both directions** before the run.
- Pins green in both states are regression guards — name them, ⛔ never count them as red-before evidence.
- ⛔ `refuse ≠ pass`; `in_progress` is not `success`; `cancelled` is not `success`.
- ⭐ Prove the instrument produces a positive before trusting its negative — R36's first landing did this with a canary and it is the reason its negative results are worth anything.

### Standing repo rules

- **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectstack-11932 -b claude/issue-11932-compound-publish-door main && cd ../objectstack-11932 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`**; ⛔ **never edit `content/docs/releases/`**.
- ⛔ **Do not edit the TEST_DEBT / type-check-debt ledger** — #11788 owns it this round, and raising an entry to absorb your own errors is the gate-weakening floor.
- ⛔ **`packages/spec` is read-only** — `domain:spec`'s single-owner surface.
- **One changeset** — a new public route; ⛔ `skip-changeset` is wrong. It must name the route, its arity, and what it now makes possible.
- Verify against `origin/main`; re-derive the gate family from your **actual** change set and **again if it grows** (a ledger commit did exactly that twice in R35). `check:route-envelope` and `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` are in this file's family.
- ⛔ Do not mark the PR ready, do not enable auto-merge.

⛔ **`finding` is for OBSERVATION-class items only.** Concrete measured defects filed **unlabelled**, no `domain:*`, no type.

**PM (domain:cli seat) — PR #12105 is CI RED; handover agent dispatched, card stays in flight**

`Lint & Repo Gates` (job `97745771073`) on head `efd007b7`, `check:objectql-double-limit`:

```
x ObjectQL double `limit` conformance (1 problem(s)):

  - packages/rest/src/meta-compound-publish-door.test.ts: NEW ObjectQL `find` double
    that does not hold the caller's bound (1 blind, 0 breaking a shape rule, 0 unjudged).
      line 175: BLIND
      Apply the caller's bound AFTER the filter, by PRESENCE:
        const page = typeof opts?.limit === 'number' ? rows.slice(0, opts.limit) : rows;
      or make the double THROW when it is handed a bound it does not implement.
      The baseline never grows.
```

In scope and this PR's own: the offending double is in the test file this change adds.

**Why it was not caught locally, which is the part worth fixing.** The PR body quotes ~40 derived gates' verdict lines, and `check:objectql-double-limit` is **not among them** — the local gate family was re-derived three times as the change set grew, and this gate still did not come out of it. So the handover order does not stop at the one failure CI named: it re-derives the family against the actual change set and runs it through, on the reasoning that a family that missed one gate may have missed others, and CI shards can hide a second red behind the first.

**Remedies, ranked behind a measurement rather than picked by taste.** The gate prints two legal exits; which is right depends on a fact neither I nor the gate has: *does any caller in this suite actually hand that double a bound?*

- Some caller does ⇒ apply the bound after the filter by presence. It then implements real behaviour.
- No caller does ⇒ ⭐ prefer making the double **throw**. Applying a bound nothing passes is dead code, while throwing states the fake's truth — "I do not implement bounds" — and fails loudly the day a test starts relying on it instead of silently handing back every row.

⛔ Out of bounds, and named as such in the order: growing the baseline (the gate's own words are **"The baseline never grows"** — raising it is the gate-weakening floor, a maintainer decision), skipping or loosening the gate, and editing `scripts/check-objectql-double-limit.mjs`.

`needs:contract-review` stays hung on both carriers. ⛔ This seat does not clear it, does not flip the PR out of draft, and does not enable auto-merge. Review of the change itself waits for a converged head.

The PR stays draft, auto-merge stays off, and this comment clears nothing.

## CI, per job

32 check runs on `2326dd5d`, all `completed`: **31 `success`, 1 `skipped`** (`Console Pin Gate`). Nothing `in_progress`, nothing `cancelled`.

## The red, and the fix — verified from the diff, not the report

The fix is **one file, 36 insertions / 1 deletion**, and it took the refusal branch:

```ts
async find(table: string, o?: { where?: …; limit?: number }) {
    if (o?.limit !== undefined) {
        throw new Error(`fake engine: unsupported bound limit=… — this double does not implement paging`);
    }
```

⭐ **Presence, not truthiness** — `!== undefined`, so `limit: 0` (a request for *nothing*) also refuses instead of falling through as falsy and being answered with the whole table. That distinction is the one a hand-written guard usually drops.

**Why refusal rather than the `slice()` the gate offers first, and why that is a reading rather than a preference.** The choice was put behind a measurement: with the double instrumented at the seam and the suite run whole, **18 `find` calls, every one carrying `typeof o.limit === 'undefined'` — zero with a bound**, against **54 `findOne` calls recorded in the same run as the control**. No caller passes a bound, so a `slice()` branch would be a line this suite never executes, and dead code cannot be relied on to be right the day it finally runs. The throw states what the fake is, and turns "some case starts passing a bound" into a red rather than a quiet full scan that reads exactly like a pass. It also matches the file's existing idiom — `match` already throws on unsupported combinators.

⭐ **The control group was load-bearing, not decoration.** The first probe wrote through `console.error`, which vitest swallowed, and returned **0 for the bound count *and* 0 for the control**. A zero with no control is not a reading. Switching to `appendFileSync` produced the table above. That is the difference between "no caller passes a bound" and "the instrument is broken", and it was caught rather than shipped.

⛔ The baseline was not grown (the gate's own words: *"The baseline never grows"*), the gate was not skipped or loosened, and `scripts/check-objectql-double-limit.mjs` was not touched. The census moved in the only direction a real fix moves it: `(0 refuse) / 169 blind` → `(1 refuse) / 168 blind`.

## ⚠️ Two structural findings the fix surfaced — worth more than the red itself

1. **`check:objectql-double-limit` does not exist on this branch.** It landed on `main` after the branch was cut, so `dispatch-gates.mjs` — which derives the family from *the tree it is standing on* — could not name it, and did not, across three re-derivations. CI sees it because CI tests the **merge**. That is a silent blind spot for every branch behind main, not an oversight by this dev.
2. **46 gates never ran on this PR at all.** The ESLint job runs sequentially and aborts at the first failure; `check:where-matcher` had passed before the failing step, so everything after it was skipped. The dev ran the ones this change set could touch — all `exit=0`, no further reds — but the general shape stands.

Both are being filed as a `finding` (unassigned, ungraded — grading is triage's, and triage's own Routine is still stalled per #12099).

## Process honesty worth recording

The dev's probe script used a relative path in its `trap`, and the restore leg **failed** (`pathspec … did not match`) because the script had `cd`'d into `packages/rest` first. It was caught by reading `git status`, restored by hand, and confirmed by a marker count of 0 — ⛔ not by an editing tool's exit code. Every subsequent reading was taken on the verified-clean tree. A restore that silently fails is how a measurement ends up describing the wrong code.

## What remains

Only the contract verdict. When it lands here, arming is: clear the label on **both** carriers (read-modify-write + read-back), ⛔ re-read CI after the label write, then ready + auto-merge SQUASH.
